title: Magnetic control of waveguide modes with an anisotropic all-dielectric spacer
content:
by Illia Fedorin

We study how magnetic bias and passive dielectric anisotropy control the mode spectrum of a parallel-plate waveguide with a ferrite–semiconductor effective core. A subwavelength dielectric laminate supplies distinct normal and tangential spacer permittivities. The core follows a published diagonal Bloch model, and regular characteristic determinants enforce the perfect electric conductor and material-interface conditions for transverse-magnetic (TM) and transverse-electric (TE) fields. A matched scalar spacer isolates the normal-permittivity contribution: TE spectra coincide, while the TM propagation constant changes. At a plate separation of 0.4 mm, angular frequency 1011 rad/s, core fill fraction f = 0.5, compositions δ = ρ = 0.5, and bias 2500 Oe, the normalized TM constants are 3.563 and 7.944 for the laminate and scalar control. Independent finite-element calculations reproduce seven selected modal constants within 0.0026%. Bulk transfer-matrix comparisons quantify the influence of the core period and gyrotropic reduction; low-order TM examples show substantially closer agreement than the selected resonant and high-order branches. The representative TM root persists under the tested one-at-a-time parameter changes of up to 5%, with a maximum index change of 7.00%. Magnetic tuning from 2500 to 2650 Oe gives a lossless π-phase length of 30.02 mm. Complex-mode continuation connects this phase response to constituent damping and a literature-based collision-rate scenario. The results identify useful design comparisons and the material and scale conditions governing their interpretation.
author: Illia Fedorin
